youtube.baslik: How do you tell complete from partial recovery in sudden hearing loss? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: Per the 2019 guideline of the American Academy of Otolaryngology, complete recovery means thresholds return to about 10 dB of the healthy ear, with a similar word score. Improvement of more than 10 dB that is not complete is called partial recovery, and a change of less than 10 dB is defined as no recovery. In the example case, the pure-tone average improved by about 30 dB but is not within 10 dB of the healthy ear; this is partial recovery.

cumleler: How do you tell complete from partial recovery in sudden hearing loss?
The guideline names recovery after sudden loss in three ways.
Complete: thresholds return to within about ten decibels of the healthy ear.
Improvement over ten decibels that is not complete is partial recovery.
A change under ten decibels is defined as no recovery.
In the example, the average improved thirty decibels, but recovery is partial.
